symptom: On Mendix 11.17 a workflow with boundary events written by mxcli did not match what Studio Pro stores: 11.17 moved Activity.BoundaryEvents into Activity.BoundaryEventContainers, and a microflow's NotifyNotificationBoundaryEventTarget renamed its BoundaryEvent key to Activity.
file: modelsdk/canon/boundarycontainers.go (RaiseBoundaryEventContainers in mpr storageFormFor; LowerBoundaryEventContainers in GetRawUnit, mprread.decodeUnits, OpenWorkflowForMutation); canon/persistentid.go hasDuplicatePersistentID
cause: The 11.17 metamodel wraps each event in a Workflows$BoundaryEventContainer whose flow starts with an X$BoundaryEventActivity (with Annotation, Name, RelativeMiddlePoint/Size '0;0'); timers get generated names boundaryEvent1..N; the container and its event activity share one PersistentId.
fix: Writers and readers keep the 11.16 shape. Storage normalization raises to the 11.17 shape before canon.Reconcile, so the transplant compares like with like; every reader lowers. Timer names survive the lowering, are read into BoundaryEvent.Name, written back, and carried by create or modify. The duplicate-PersistentId check skips the container's copy, which otherwise aborted the whole PersistentId carry.
insight: No Studio Pro example was needed to start: mx convert from an 11.16 project holding every event kind gives the exact target shape, and the registry main.js schema names the properties. Test the raise as raise(11.16 unit) == converted unit, minus $IDs. A shared identity value the target format introduces deliberately will trip every 'no duplicates' guard downstream; look for them (here hasDuplicatePersistentID) when a write suddenly mints fresh IDs.
test: modelsdk/canon/boundarycontainers_2616_test.go (raise matches mx convert for workflow and notify; lower-then-raise is the stored unit; no-op below 11.17; PersistentId carry survives the shared ID), mdl/executor/workflow_carry_boundary_names_2616_test.go; all comparisons fail with the raise disabled
